title: Calculate Direct Report Counts per Manager
description_markdown: For each manager who manages at least one employee in `employees`, count their total direct reports as `reports_count`. Return `manager_id`, `COUNT(*) AS reports_count`. Order by `reports_count` DESC, `manager_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Count direct reports per manager
SELECT manager_id, COUNT(*) AS reports_count
FROM employees
WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ...
solution_query: SELECT manager_id, COUNT(*) AS reports_count FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY manager_id ORDER BY reports_count DESC, manager_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates the subordinate distribution across managers.
hints: Group by `manager_id` and count rows.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT manager_id, COUNT(*) AS reports_count FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY manager_id ORDER BY reports_count DESC, manager_id ASC;

title: Traverse Corporate Leadership Rollup
description_markdown: Using a recursive CTE starting at the CEO (`emp_id = 1`), find all employees in the CEO's management tree. Return their `emp_id`, `first_name`, `salary`, and their distance from the CEO as `depth`. Order by `depth` ASC, `emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Recursive subtree query
WITH RECURSIVE ceo_tree AS (
  ...
)
SELECT ...
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE ceo_tree AS (SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 0 AS depth FROM employees WHERE emp_id = 1 UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.salary, ct.depth + 1 FROM employees e JOIN ceo_tree ct ON e.manager_id = ct.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, depth FROM ceo_tree ORDER BY depth ASC, emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Recursively unwinds the entire subordinate tree starting from the top executive anchor node.
hints: Anchor: `SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 0 AS depth FROM employees WHERE emp_id = 1`.
Recursive join: `JOIN ceo_tree ct ON e.manager_id = ct.emp_id`.

Query: WITH RECURSIVE ceo_tree AS (SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 0 AS depth FROM employees WHERE emp_id = 1 UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.salary, ct.depth + 1 FROM employees e JOIN ceo_tree ct ON e.manager_id = ct.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, depth FROM ceo_tree ORDER BY depth ASC, emp_id ASC;

title: Build Breadcrumb Line of Management String
description_markdown: Use a recursive CTE to build a breadcrumb reporting string `management_path` for every employee starting with their own name and prepending managers up to the CEO (e.g. 'Eleanor Vance > Marcus Brody > Sophia Chen'). Return `emp_id`, `first_name`, and `management_path`. Order by `emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Recursive path concatenation
WITH RECURSIVE path_tree AS (
  ...
)
SELECT ...
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE path_tree AS (SELECT emp_id, first_name, CAST(first_name AS CHAR(255)) AS management_path FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, CONCAT(pt.management_path, ' > ', e.first_name) FROM employees e JOIN path_tree pt ON e.manager_id = pt.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, first_name, management_path FROM path_tree ORDER BY emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Constructs an organizational pedigree breadcrumb path using recursive CONCAT and CAST to CHAR(255) for MySQL length expansion.
common_mistakes: Using || for string concatenation instead of MySQL CONCAT().
Forgetting to CAST the initial anchor column to CHAR(255) to prevent string truncation in MySQL.
dialect_notes: In MySQL recursive CTEs, string columns must be cast in the anchor member (e.g. CAST(col AS CHAR(255))) to prevent width truncation.
hints: Anchor on root nodes (`manager_id IS NULL`) with `CAST(first_name AS CHAR(255)) AS management_path`.
Concatenate in recursive step: `CONCAT(pt.management_path, ' > ', e.first_name)`.

Query: WITH RECURSIVE path_tree AS (SELECT emp_id, first_name, CAST(first_name AS CHAR(255)) AS management_path FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, CONCAT(pt.management_path, ' > ', e.first_name) FROM employees e JOIN path_tree pt ON e.manager_id = pt.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, first_name, management_path FROM path_tree ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

title: Identify Top-Level Organization Executive with No Manager

starter_query:
-- Find root organization executive
SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, job_title
FROM employees
WHERE manager_id IS NULL AND dept_id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY emp_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, job_title FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL AND dept_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

interview_tip: Root nodes anchor recursive queries and top-down org chart rollups.

Query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, job_title FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL AND dept_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

title: Count Direct Child Subcategories per Parent Category
description_markdown: From `categories`, count the number of direct child subcategories for each parent category where `parent_category_id IS NOT NULL`. Group by `parent_category_id` and alias count as `subcategory_count`. Return `parent_category_id` and `subcategory_count`. Order by `parent_category_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Direct child subcategory counts
SELECT parent_category_id, COUNT(*) AS subcategory_count

WHERE parent_category_id IS NOT NULL

ORDER BY parent_category_id ASC;

hints: Filter `WHERE parent_category_id IS NOT NULL`.
Group by `parent_category_id` and sort `parent_category_id ASC`.

title: Calculate Direct Report Headcount with Manager Names
description_markdown: Self-join `employees` as manager (`m`) and report (`e`) on `e.manager_id = m.emp_id`. Calculate each manager's direct report count as `direct_reports`. Return `m.emp_id AS manager_id`, `m.first_name AS manager_name`, and `direct_reports`. Order by `direct_reports` DESC, `m.emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Direct report headcount per manager with names
SELECT m.emp_id AS manager_id, m.first_name AS manager_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports
FROM employees m
JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id
GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.first_name
ORDER BY direct_reports DESC, m.emp_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT m.emp_id AS manager_id, m.first_name AS manager_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports FROM employees m JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.first_name ORDER BY direct_reports DESC, m.emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Self-joining parent and child records attaches manager attributes to aggregated report counts.
common_mistakes: Swapping the join condition and counting managers per employee.
interview_tip: Manager span-of-control is a classic organizational engineering metric.
hints: Join `employees m` with `employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id`.
Group by `m.emp_id, m.first_name`.

Query: SELECT m.emp_id AS manager_id, m.first_name AS manager_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports FROM employees m JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.first_name ORDER BY direct_reports DESC, m.emp_id ASC;

title: Identify Leaf Individual Contributors with No Direct Reports
description_markdown: From `employees`, identify all leaf-level staff (individual contributors) who do not manage any employees (`emp_id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL)`). Return `emp_id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, and `job_title`. Order by `emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Leaf employees with no direct reports
SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, job_title
FROM employees
WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY emp_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, job_title FROM employees WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Leaf nodes in a hierarchy are keys that never appear as parents in the relationship table.
common_mistakes: Omitting WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL in the NOT IN subquery, which would cause NOT IN to evaluate to UNKNOWN.
interview_tip: Always filter out NULLs when using NOT IN subqueries to avoid three-valued logic pitfalls.
hints: Use `WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL)`.
Sort output by `emp_id ASC`.
Query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, last_name, job_title FROM employees WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

title: Traverse Engineering Management Subtree with Relative Depth
description_markdown: Using a recursive CTE rooted at the VP of Engineering (`emp_id = 2`), traverse the entire engineering organizational subtree. Start with `level = 0` for Marcus, and increment `level + 1` for each subsequent management tier. Return `emp_id`, `first_name`, `job_title`, and `level`. Order by `level` ASC, `emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Recursive engineering subtree traversal
WITH RECURSIVE eng_tree AS (
  SELECT emp_id, first_name, job_title, 0 AS level
  FROM employees
  WHERE emp_id = 2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.job_title, et.level + 1
  FROM employees e
  JOIN eng_tree et ON e.manager_id = et.emp_id
)
SELECT emp_id, first_name, job_title, level
FROM eng_tree
ORDER BY level ASC, emp_id ASC;
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE eng_tree AS (SELECT emp_id, first_name, job_title, 0 AS level FROM employees WHERE emp_id = 2 UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.job_title, et.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN eng_tree et ON e.manager_id = et.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, first_name, job_title, level FROM eng_tree ORDER BY level ASC, emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Recursive CTE anchors on Marcus Brody and cascades down through direct and indirect reports.
common_mistakes: Joining on e.emp_id = et.manager_id instead of e.manager_id = et.emp_id.
interview_tip: Downward recursive traversal tracks departmental reach and chain-of-command depth.
hints: Anchor on `emp_id = 2` with `0 AS level`.
Recursive join: `JOIN eng_tree et ON e.manager_id = et.emp_id`.

Query: WITH RECURSIVE eng_tree AS (SELECT emp_id, first_name, job_title, 0 AS level FROM employees WHERE emp_id = 2 UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.job_title, et.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN eng_tree et ON e.manager_id = et.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, first_name, job_title, level FROM eng_tree ORDER BY level ASC, emp_id ASC;

title: Traverse Full Catalog Category Taxonomy Hierarchy with Depth
description_markdown: Using a recursive CTE starting at all root categories (`parent_category_id IS NULL` at `depth = 0`), traverse all subcategories and compute each category's depth level in the taxonomy. Return `category_id`, `category_name`, and `depth`. Order by `depth` ASC, `category_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Recursive catalog taxonomy depth
WITH RECURSIVE cat_tree AS (
  SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, 0 AS depth
  FROM categories
  WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, ct.depth + 1
  FROM categories c
  JOIN cat_tree ct ON c.parent_category_id = ct.category_id
)
SELECT category_id, category_name, depth
FROM cat_tree
ORDER BY depth ASC, category_id ASC;
solution_query: WITH RECURSIVE cat_tree AS (SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, 0 AS depth FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, ct.depth + 1 FROM categories c JOIN cat_tree ct ON c.parent_category_id = ct.category_id) SELECT category_id, category_name, depth FROM cat_tree ORDER BY depth ASC, category_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Multiple root nodes can anchor a recursive CTE concurrently, producing depth tiers across all catalog branches.
common_mistakes: Restricting the anchor to only one root category instead of all categories with parent_category_id IS NULL.
interview_tip: Multi-root recursive queries elegantly handle forests (collections of disjoint trees).
hints: Anchor on all rows `WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL`.
Recurse by joining `c.parent_category_id = ct.category_id`.

title: Filter Managers with at Least Two Direct Reports
description_markdown: Self-join `employees` as `m` (manager) and `e` (report). Find all managers who have at least 2 direct reports (`COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 2`). Return `m.emp_id AS manager_id`, `m.first_name AS manager_name`, and `COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports`. Order by `direct_reports` DESC, `m.emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Managers with >= 2 direct reports
SELECT m.emp_id AS manager_id, m.first_name AS manager_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports
FROM employees m
JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id
GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.first_name
HAVING COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 2
ORDER BY direct_reports DESC, m.emp_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT m.emp_id AS manager_id, m.first_name AS manager_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports FROM employees m JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.first_name HAVING COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 2 ORDER BY direct_reports DESC, m.emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: HAVING filters managers by minimum supervisory load.
common_mistakes: Using WHERE COUNT(...) instead of HAVING.
interview_tip: Organizations monitor minimum team sizes to avoid overly thin managerial ratios.
hints: Use `HAVING COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 2`.
Sort by `direct_reports DESC, m.emp_id ASC`.

Query: SELECT m.emp_id AS manager_id, m.first_name AS manager_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports FROM employees m JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.first_name HAVING COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 2 ORDER BY direct_reports DESC, m.emp_id ASC;

title: Display Every Subordinate Alongside Their Immediate Manager Name
description_markdown: From `employees`, join every employee `e` with their immediate supervisor `m` on `e.manager_id = m.emp_id`. Return `e.emp_id`, `e.first_name`, `e.last_name`, and `m.first_name AS manager_first_name`. Order by `e.emp_id` ASC.

title: Calculate Employee Headcount Distribution Across Hierarchy Depth Levels
description_markdown: Using a recursive CTE starting at the root CEO (`manager_id IS NULL AND dept_id IS NOT NULL` at `depth = 0`), calculate the hierarchy depth of every employee. WITH RECURSIVE org AS (

  FROM employees e
  JOIN org o ON e.manager_id = o.emp_id
)
SELECT depth, COUNT(*) AS employee_count
FROM org
GROUP BY depth
ORDER BY depth ASC;

title: Calculate Department Headcount and Active Manager Counts

-- Department management density

title: Calculate Maximum Hierarchy Depth Level Across Departments
